title: First Production Launch Checklist — QA Plan (Hosted API MVP)
body:
Owner: Leila Farouk (QA)
Reviewers/DRIs: Dylan Brooks (Console), Logan Wright (Telemetry), Monica Patel (SDK), Nadia Rahman (pipeline), Wei Chen (Docs/Quickstarts)
Last updated: 2025-04-05

Purpose
- Validate the “First Production Launch” checklist end-to-end for Hosted API: UI state, progress persistence, event emission, and KPI attribution.
- Catch regressions that cause the most onboarding tickets: auth mistakes (401/403), rate limit (429) confusion, streaming disconnect confusion, and usage dashboard lag/mismatch.
- Ensure consistent behavior across regions and SDKs before cohort rollout.

Scope (MVP)
In scope
1) Console checklist UI
- Entry points (home/dashboard banner + onboarding section)
- Step list + step detail drawer
- Deep links to Console pages and docs
- States: Not started, In progress, Completed, Blocked/Needs attention (if present), Hidden when FF off
- Error/empty states (telemetry unavailable, tenant missing)

2) Progress tracking + eventing
- Server-side onboarding event emission (gateway/control plane)
- Progress service ingestion + derived step completion
- Idempotency and ordering (post ENG-5866 fix)

3) SDK/quickstart flows
- Python, TypeScript, Go SDK paths
- OpenAI-compat layer attribution (user-agent tagging)
- Streaming happy path and streaming reconnect guidance
- Production defaults where implemented (timeouts/retries)

4) Analytics sanity checks (not full BI validation)
- Events appear in dataset and dashboard within expected freshness window
- TTFS/TTFP computed for test tenants without obvious mis-attribution

Out of scope (MVP)
- Full guided tours (tooltips/walkthrough overlays)
- Dedicated/Private onboarding
- Automated remediation suggestions

Release gating / exit criteria
- 0 P0 bugs open; <= 3 P1 bugs with documented mitigation and Support macro updates.
- All “Happy Path” test cases pass across 3 regions and top 3 SDKs.
- No step regressions observed under out-of-order/duplicate event tests.
- Feature flag kill switch works: checklist fully hidden and progress service calls stopped (or gracefully no-op) when disabled.

Test environments / dependencies
- Console: staging + prod (dogfood cohort)
- Gateway/control plane: staging + prod (dogfood)
- Progress service: staging + prod
- Telemetry pipeline: staging dataset + prod dataset
- Feature flag: onboarding_checklist_enabled (name per PR-28467; confirm exact flag key before execution)

Regions to validate
- us-east-1
- us-west-2
- eu-central-1

SDKs / clients to validate
- Redwood SDK: Python
- Redwood SDK: TypeScript
- Redwood SDK: Go
- OpenAI-compat: redwood-openai-compat (user-agent tags)

Browsers (Console)
- Chrome latest
- Safari latest (macOS)
- Firefox latest

Test tenant setup
NOTE: do not paste secrets into this doc. API keys stored in 1Password “DevEx QA - Onboarding Checklist” vault.

Naming convention
- Tenants: qa-onboarding-<region>-<sdk>-<date>
- Projects/routes: default route named “qa-checklist-route”
- Model: use a stable small model for speed/cost (confirm current recommended default model in docs)

Test accounts (initial set)
1) qa-onboarding-use1-python
- Region: us-east-1
- SDK: Python
- Console role: Org Admin (needed for API key + quotas)
- Intended for full happy path + most failure modes

2) qa-onboarding-usw2-ts
- Region: us-west-2
- SDK: TypeScript
- Intended for streaming + retry/backoff tests

3) qa-onboarding-euc1-go
- Region: eu-central-1
- SDK: Go
- Intended for networking/streaming disconnect simulation and latency sensitivity

4) qa-onboarding-use1-openai-compat
- Region: us-east-1
- Client: OpenAI-compat layer
- Intended for attribution and event emission validation (user-agent tags)

Checklist steps under test (MVP mapping)
We validate that each step can transition to Completed based on expected events OR explicit user actions, and cannot regress.
Expected step list (subject to final copy):
S1 Create API key
S2 Configure environment (env var / config)
S3 Make first successful request (2xx)
S4 Try streaming
S5 Add production-safe retries/timeouts
S6 Review usage & latency dashboard
S7 Set quotas/budgets (or understand limits)
S8 Pin model version
S9 Configure fallback policy (model/region)
S10 Add observability hooks (request ID / tracing)

Event validation
Source of truth for completion is server-side events (per ADR). For QA we validate:
- Event emitted at correct moment
- Required fields present
- No PII in payload
- Cardinality constraints are respected (e.g., model name allowed; prompt text NOT allowed)
- Idempotency keys prevent duplicate state transitions

Expected event names (confirm against schema v1)
Use these as QA targets; if final names differ, update this doc and test scripts.
- onboarding.api_key.created
- onboarding.env_config.detected (optional; only if we emit client hints)
- onboarding.request.first_success (first 2xx)
- onboarding.streaming.first_established
- onboarding.retries_timeouts.configured (may be derived; see notes)
- onboarding.usage_dashboard.viewed (Console event)
- onboarding.quota_budget.configured
- onboarding.model.pinned
- onboarding.fallback.configured
- onboarding.observability.enabled

Important: Some steps may be derived or may only be tracked by Console events (e.g., “viewed usage dashboard”). Validate the source per step in the PRD/UX spec during execution.

How to verify events
Staging
- Use telemetry staging query (Logan/Nadia can provide saved query) filtering by tenant_id.
- Verify event_count and ordering by emitted_at.

Prod dogfood
- Use “Onboarding KPIs” dashboard filter by tenant_id (or internal tenant label).
- Cross-check raw event stream (internal admin viewer) if dashboard lags.

Data freshness expectations
- Raw events visible within 2–5 minutes.
- Dashboard aggregation within 15–60 minutes (depending on pipeline; track actual during QA).
- Known limitation: usage dashboard may lag; ensure checklist copy and support macros mention expected delay.

Test matrix overview
We execute:
- Happy path: per SDK x region (at least 1 each, with Python covering full flow)
- Failure modes: primarily on Python tenant + streaming on TS/Go
- Feature flag behavior: staging + prod cohort toggles

Test cases

A. Feature flag gating
A1 Checklist hidden when flag OFF
Steps
1) Ensure tenant is not in enabled cohort; turn flag off.
2) Load Console home.
Expected
- No checklist entry point, no checklist API calls (or calls return 404/disabled with graceful UI).
- No onboarding Console analytics events emitted.

A2 Checklist visible when flag ON
Steps
1) Add tenant to enabled cohort (or enable flag globally in staging).
2) Load Console home.
Expected
- Checklist visible; initial state loads.
- Empty state handled if no progress yet.

A3 Kill switch behavior under load
Steps
1) With checklist visible, refresh and navigate between pages.
2) Disable flag mid-session.
Expected
- Checklist disappears or becomes “disabled” per UX; no console errors; no infinite polling.


B. Happy path completion (per SDK)
B1 Python happy path (us-east-1)
Pre-req
- Tenant is enabled.
Steps
1) Create API key in Console.
2) Set env var locally (REDWOOD_API_KEY or equivalent).
3) Run minimal “hello world” completion/chat request.
4) Run streaming chat request (SSE/websocket per SDK).
5) Enable recommended retries/timeouts preset in SDK.
6) Open Usage dashboard and Latency dashboard.
7) Configure quota/budget alert (if available in Console for this tenant) OR confirm step completion criteria.
8) Pin model version on route.
9) Configure fallback policy (at least one fallback model/region) and save.
10) Add request-id logging and (if available) tracing header propagation.
Expected
- Checklist step transitions:
  - S1 completes after api_key.created observed.
  - S3 completes after first 2xx observed (check event has route/model fields).
  - S4 completes after streaming established (not merely a request with stream=true that fails).
  - Remaining steps complete based on their defined signals.
- Steps never regress upon refresh.
- Deep links navigate to correct Console pages.
- Docs links open canonical checklist docs pages.

B2 TypeScript happy path (us-west-2)
Focus
- Streaming + retries/timeouts
- Browser console should show no errors
Expected
- Same as B1 for S1–S5 at minimum.

B3 Go happy path (eu-central-1)
Focus
- Streaming reconnect helper behavior (if included)
- Network variability simulation (see failure tests)

B4 OpenAI-compat happy path (us-east-1)
Focus
- User-agent tagging results in correct attribution; events still emitted server-side.
Expected
- onboarding.request.first_success triggers via compat layer calls
- No missing required fields due to compat translation


C. Failure modes (support-ticket driven)
C1 401 Invalid API key
Steps
1) Use an invalid or revoked key in SDK.
2) Make request.
Expected
- Request fails with 401.
- Checklist does NOT complete “first success”.
- If we emit an auth_failure event, verify it does not contain key material.
- Console step detail copy helps user fix (links to API key docs).

C2 403 Forbidden (org mismatch / wrong project)
Steps
1) Use a key from another tenant (QA-only scenario).
2) Make request.
Expected
- 403; no “first success”.
- Support macro notes: ask user to confirm org + env var.

C3 429 Rate limit on early load
Steps
1) Lower quota artificially (or use load test to exceed).
2) Make burst of requests.
Expected
- 429 responses.
- Checklist should surface “configure quotas/budgets” as incomplete (or “needs attention” if supported).
- Docs link points to quota/backoff guidance.
- Verify we do not mark “production readiness” steps complete due to 429.

C4 Streaming disconnect mid-response
Steps
1) Start streaming request.
2) Simulate disconnect (kill process / drop network).
3) Retry with reconnect helper (TS/Go) or manual restart.
Expected
- Streaming step completion only after first successful stream established; disconnect should not regress completion.
- No duplicate streaming established events cause state flip-flop.
- Copy links to streaming disconnect guide.

C5 Request timeout
Steps
1) Force a very low timeout.
2) Make request.
Expected
- Client sees timeout; server may still process.
- Ensure we do not incorrectly count it as first success unless server returned 2xx (event-driven).
- Retry guidance step should remain incomplete until configured.

C6 Dashboard lag / mismatch
Steps
1) Make requests.
2) Immediately open Usage dashboard.
Expected
- If usage data lags, Console messaging should indicate delay.
- Checklist step “Review usage dashboard” should either (a) complete on page view regardless of freshness, or (b) not complete; confirm intended behavior.
- File issue if users likely to interpret lag as “not working”.


D. Event ordering / idempotency / race conditions (ENG-5866)
D1 Out-of-order delivery
Method
- Use test harness or internal tool to replay events out of order for same tenant (Logan/Nadia to assist).
Scenario
- streaming.first_established arrives before request.first_success.
Expected
- Progress service should compute monotonic completion; final state should mark both complete once both events exist.
- No regression from Completed -> In progress.

D2 Duplicate events
Scenario
- Same onboarding.request.first_success emitted twice with same idempotency key.
Expected
- One state transition; audit log shows dedupe (if visible).

D3 Partial ingestion failure
Scenario
- Temporarily block progress ingestion endpoint in staging (or simulate 5xx) while gateway emits.
Expected
- Console shows “temporarily unavailable” state and recovers after pipeline resumes.
- No permanent loss; replay/backfill behavior documented.


E. Admin override + audit trail (Support tooling)
E1 Mark step complete (Support/admin)
Steps
1) Use admin override endpoint/tool to mark step as complete with reason “QA test”.
2) Refresh Console.
Expected
- Step shows complete with “set by admin” indicator (if UX includes) and audit trail recorded.
- Normal events after override do not break state.

E2 Reset step
Steps
1) Reset a completed step.
Expected
- Step returns to incomplete.
- Subsequent new event can re-complete.


F. Security/privacy checks (quick QA)
F1 Payload PII scan
Steps
1) Inspect sample events for test tenant.
Expected
- No prompt text, no raw messages, no email, no API key fragments.
- Only allowed identifiers: tenant_id, project_id/route_id, model_id/model_slug, region, sdk name/version, request_id (opaque).

F2 Data residency
Steps
1) For EU tenant, verify storage/processing meets residency constraints as documented (at minimum, events show region tag and follow expected pipeline).
Expected
- No unexpected cross-region storage flags (raise to Marcus Lin if uncertain).


Execution checklist (per run)
1) Confirm flag status and cohort assignment.
2) Confirm tenant region.
3) Confirm SDK version (record git SHA or released version).
4) Perform steps; screenshot checklist before/after major transitions.
5) Verify raw events (within 5 min).
6) Verify checklist state matches expected completion.
7) Verify dashboard aggregates within expected window.
8) File issues with severity + repro steps + tenant_id + approximate timestamps.

What to record for every bug
- Tenant name + tenant_id
- Region
- SDK + version
- Console URL and affected step
- Timestamp range (UTC)
- Expected vs actual step state
- Raw event snippet (redacted) and event_id/idempotency_key if available

Open questions / watch-outs
- Step definitions: Some steps (e.g., “retries/timeouts configured”) may not have a deterministic server-side signal. Confirm final completion criteria with DevEx/Telemetry before calling it a bug.
- Usage dashboard delay: ensure copy aligns with reality; otherwise customers will file “not counting usage” tickets.
- Model pinning/fallback: verify tenant permissions; some plans may not expose these settings. If hidden, checklist must adapt (don’t show impossible steps).

Known issues observed during dogfood (as of 2025-03-21)
- Occasional step regression after refresh (likely out-of-order event handling) — verify fix from PR-28510.
- Deep link mismatch for quotas page in EU region (URL routing issue) — re-test.

Next actions
- Leila: run A/B/C tests on staging by 2025-04-07.
- Dylan/Chloe: confirm final step list + mapping to event names.
- Logan/Nadia: provide saved queries for staging/prod event validation and expected freshness SLA.
- Monica/Ibrahim: confirm SDK versions included in rollout cohort and update recommended retry/timeout presets in quickstarts.
